title: Public storage bucket listing enabled on cdn.dreamdex.io
CSP report-only header on app.testnet responses discloses internal dev/staging hosts
Unauthenticated /metrics on api.testnet.dreamdex.io exposes internal route table and traffic stats
State-changing POST /api/sponsor/warm accepts unauthenticated calls without rate limiting
Market Data docs promise unknown symbols are silently skipped (empty []), live API returns 400 invalid_param
Market Data docs show comma-separated symbols returning [], live API parses both symbols (200 with data)
WS operations with missing parameters return a REST-style 404 bad_request envelope instead of the documented invalid_parameters protocol error
Error Handling table documents error name invalid_interval, live API returns invalid_param for the same case

Perps developer page documents chain 50383 while the HTTP API and Contract Addresses page describe a different deployment on 50312; two of the six documented addresses resolve to a different contract there
Trader docs list 21 markets as BTC-PERP style names; the REST registry serves BASE:USDso and 404s every -PERP name, including markets whose base ticker it does carry
HTTP API base-URL table sends testnet developers to stg.api.dreamdex.io; the perps API host api.testnet.dreamdex.io is undocumented anywhere
NUL byte in the URL path returns 400 with empty body and no Error-Name header, violating the documented JSON error contract
POST /v0/auth/login with a non-JSON Content-Type returns 500 internal_error and leaks a V8 exception string
Cancel and reduce prepares return calldata for an order id that does not exist
Leverage endpoint accepts values far above the documented per-market maximum while amount validation enforces the documented minimum
Nine of twenty-four perps pools have no stop-order registry while the docs advertise TP/SL on every market
Three pools sit outside the insurance-fund tier while the docs present the Insurance Fund as the standard ladder stage
Voucher distributor campaign is over with zero budget and claim() reverts while the docs still promise any address can claim 1,000 USDso
One EOA owns every core perps contract and the shared pool beacon
No perps contract has published source on the explorer
App redirects every visitor to a default market that does not exist in the API registry
App ships a 10m candle interval option that the candles endpoint and its own OpenAPI spec reject
Bot kit ships with a default spot symbol that does not exist on the testnet it targets
Same malformed WebSocket frame returns two different validator messages on the two hosts the kit and docs call "testnet"
One WebSocket feed is published under three different path shapes and the spec's own path variant with a trailing slash 404s
Numeric input overflows return 500/503 that leak internal library versions, package names and RPC method names
Order endpoints accept a 5MB JSON body, answer 500 instead of 413, and echo ~10MB back
Known routes answer unsupported HTTP methods with 404 bad_request instead of 405
PATCH with no body and no Content-Type reports invalid_amount instead of invalid_request_body
Duplicate JSON keys in an order request are accepted silently (last-key-wins) and produce calldata
Query parameter validation is lax: limit accepts non-integer syntax and unknown/negative params are silently ignored
404 envelopes use an undocumented error name and skip the Error-Name header the docs promise
Margin deposit ignores the currency parameter entirely while the market vault rejects the same values
Rate limiting only trips after high-RPS bursts and every 429 advertises Retry-After: 1
gzip-compressed request body is rejected as invalid JSON instead of 415 Unsupported Media Type
Stop-order endpoints return 404 on all 24 perp markets, including the 15 that do have a stop-order registry
WBTC and WETH are listed as both spot and perp under the identical symbol, and every write resolves to the spot market, leaving the perp side unaddressable
builder/approve encodes any max fee the caller asks for, including values above the pool cap, producing a transaction the pool always reverts
The spec declares the builder-fee ceilings as unbounded integers while every pool enforces a finite on-chain cap
vault/approve answers HTTP 200 with a literal null body for a currency the same endpoint lists as accepted
The spec's declared production WebSocket pathname 404s on production and staging while testnet accepts it, so spec-generated clients connect only on testnet
The testnet spec advertises nine subscribe channels and production recognises five, so four documented channels answer unknown_channel on mainnet
Trader docs open-interest cap is 2x or 4x the on-chain cap on 20 of 21 markets
The bot-kit ships four different DRY_RUN parsers, and the value the docs recommend makes one shipped example trade live
example-08's template .env ships DRY_RUN=0, so a copied template is a live configuration and `npm start` reflects no deliberate choice
perp-maker's link gate answers `ok: true` when there is no trading key, so it can never fail and the live bot runs on without warning
The margin status reader falls back to "Healthy" for any value outside 0-3, so an unreadable status is reported as the safest one
CHAIN_ID is a free-form override with no range check and no cross-check against the RPC, so a typo signs against one chain while reading another
